question: Does more money make people happier, and does it ever stop mattering?
title: money & happiness
hook: Does your happiness plateau once you earn enough, or does it keep climbing?
answer: Average happiness does not hit a permanent ceiling as income rises, with 41% of those in the highest family income bracket reporting they are very happy.

stats.label: of families earning over $200k say they are very happy
of the highest income tenth are satisfied with finances
average life evaluation out of ten in wealthiest nations

followups: How does marital status change the link between income and happiness?
Has our overall financial satisfaction declined over the last few decades?
Does national wealth guarantee higher life satisfaction across all global regions?
body:
## more money goes with happier lives

When you look at the global stage, richer nations report consistently higher life evaluation scores than poorer ones (WHR 2026). When countries are grouped by wealth, the average life evaluation rises steadily to **6.9** out of ten in the richest tenth of nations (WHR 2026). This climb does not flatten out, and the jump between the ninth and tenth wealth brackets represents one of the largest steps on record (WHR 2026).

```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "National life satisfaction continues to climb as countries grow richer", "y_label": "average life evaluation", "unit": "", "labels": ["Quintile 1", "Quintile 2", "Quintile 3", "Quintile 4", "Quintile 5"], "series": [{"name": "Life evaluation", "data": [4.4, 5.0, 5.6, 6.0, 6.7]}], "highlight": "Quintile 5", "note": "Averages for 2019-2025."}
```

## the local plateau is only temporary

Looking closer at households, the share of people who say they are very happy does not rise in a completely straight line (GSS 1972-2024). There is a brief stalling point between the $75,000 to $100,000 bracket and the $100,000 to $150,000 bracket where the share of very happy people remains nearly flat (GSS 1972-2024). But this ceiling is temporary, as families earning over $200,000 see their very happy share reach its peak of **41%** (GSS 1972-2024).

```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "The share of very happy people climbs again after a middle-income stall", "y_label": "share saying they are very happy", "unit": "%", "labels": ["Under $20k", "$20k-$40k", "$40k-$75k", "$75k-$100k", "$100k-$150k", "$150k-$200k", "Over $200k"], "series": [{"name": "very happy", "data": [21.72, 25.21, 28.58, 33.31, 33.68, 38.86, 41.33]}], "highlight": "Over $200k", "note": "Weighted shares, 1972-2024."}
```

## marriage shapes the income stall

This middle-income stall looks different depending on who you share your life with (GSS 1972-2024). For married couples, the share of very happy respondents remains almost completely flat at **39%** across that middle-income gap (GSS 1972-2024). Unmarried individuals actually report a slight drop in happiness before climbing again in the highest brackets (GSS 1972-2024).

```chart
{"type": "bar", "title": "Married people report higher happiness across all incomes", "y_label": "share saying they are very happy", "unit": "%", "labels": ["Under $20k", "$20k-$40k", "$40k-$75k", "$75k-$100k", "$100k-$150k", "$150k-$200k", "Over $200k"], "series": [{"name": "Married", "data": [32.60, 34.82, 36.27, 38.73, 38.82, 42.32, 44.84]}, {"name": "Not Married", "data": [18.63, 18.73, 18.87, 22.01, 20.22, 27.77, 30.28]}], "note": "Weighted shares, 1972-2024."}
```

## satisfaction peaks at the very top

Financial satisfaction tracks closely with real earnings, peaking sharply for those at the highest levels of income (GSS 1972-2024). In the highest family income bracket, 52% of people report being pretty well satisfied, compared to a much lower share in the poorest groups (GSS 1972-2024). Those in the highest tenth of earners stand out even more, with **58%** reporting they are pretty well satisfied and only 8% saying they are not satisfied at all (GSS 1972-2024).

## what this data can't tell you

While the data shows a notable drop in overall happiness and financial satisfaction during the 2020s, this may not reflect actual societal shifts. The GSS transitioned its survey format from face-to-face interviews to online and mixed-mode surveys starting in 2021. This shift in how people were asked questions can alter how they answer, meaning we cannot say for certain if Americans truly became less satisfied.

trail.task: In the GSS dataset, what is the weighted percentage of respondents who are 'very happy' (happy = 1) and the average happiness score (where 1 is very happy, 3 is not too happy) across different brackets of family_income_2024usd (e.g., under $20k, $20k-$40k, $40k-$75k, $75k-$100k, $100k-$150k, $150k-$200k, and over $200k)? Does the share of 'very happy' people plateau at higher income levels?

queries.sql: SELECT MIN(family_income_2024usd), MAX(family_income_2024usd), COUNT(*), COUNT(family_income_2024usd), COUNT(happy) FROM gss;

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 20000 THEN '1. Under $20k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 20000 AND family_income_2024usd < 40000 THEN '2. $20k-$40k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 40000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $40k-$75k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75k-$100k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100k-$150k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 AND family_income_2024usd < 200000 THEN '6. $150k-$200k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 200000 THEN '7. Over $200k'
  END AS income_bracket,
  COUNT(*) as respondent_count,
  SUM(weight) as sum_weight,
  SUM(weight * (happy = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 AS pct_very_happy,
  SUM(weight * happy) / SUM(weight) AS avg_happiness
FROM gss
WHERE happy IS NOT NULL AND family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN year < 2000 THEN 'Pre-2000'
    WHEN year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2018 THEN '2000-2018'
    ELSE '2021-2024'
  END AS era,
  CASE
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 20000 THEN '1. Under $20k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 20000 AND family_income_2024usd < 40000 THEN '2. $20k-$40k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 40000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $40k-$75k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75k-$100k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100k-$150k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 AND family_income_2024usd < 200000 THEN '6. $150k-$200k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 200000 THEN '7. Over $200k'
  END AS income_bracket,
  COUNT(*) as respondent_count,
  SUM(weight * (happy = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 AS pct_very_happy,
  SUM(weight * happy) / SUM(weight) AS avg_happiness
FROM gss
WHERE happy IS NOT NULL AND family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 20000 THEN '1. Under $20k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 20000 AND family_income_2024usd < 40000 THEN '2. $20k-$40k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 40000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $40k-$75k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75k-$100k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100k-$150k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 AND family_income_2024usd < 200000 THEN '6. $150k-$200k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 200000 THEN '7. Over $200k'
  END AS income_bracket,
  SUM(weight * (marital = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 AS pct_married
FROM gss
WHERE marital IS NOT NULL AND family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

SELECT
  CASE WHEN marital = 1 THEN 'Married' ELSE 'Not Married' END AS marital_status,
  CASE
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 20000 THEN '1. Under $20k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 20000 AND family_income_2024usd < 40000 THEN '2. $20k-$40k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 40000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $40k-$75k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75k-$100k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100k-$150k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 AND family_income_2024usd < 200000 THEN '6. $150k-$200k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 200000 THEN '7. Over $200k'
  END AS income_bracket,
  COUNT(*) as respondent_count,
  SUM(weight * (happy = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 AS pct_very_happy,
  SUM(weight * happy) / SUM(weight) AS avg_happiness
FROM gss
WHERE happy IS NOT NULL AND family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL AND marital IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1, 2
ORDER BY 1, 2;

SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 20000 THEN '1. Under $20k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 20000 AND family_income_2024usd < 40000 THEN '2. $20k-$40k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 40000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $40k-$75k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75k-$100k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100k-$150k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 AND family_income_2024usd < 200000 THEN '6. $150k-$200k'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 200000 THEN '7. Over $200k'
  END AS income_bracket,
  AVG(year) AS avg_year
FROM gss
WHERE happy IS NOT NULL AND family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

queries.sql:
SELECT 
  quantile(family_income_2024usd, 0.1) as p10,
  quantile(family_income_2024usd, 0.25) as p25,
  quantile(family_income_2024usd, 0.5) as p50,
  quantile(family_income_2024usd, 0.75) as p75,
  quantile(family_income_2024usd, 0.9) as p90
FROM gss
WHERE family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL;

SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN family_income_2024usd < 25000 THEN '1. Under $25,000'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 25000 AND family_income_2024usd < 50000 THEN '2. $25,000 - $49,999'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 50000 AND family_income_2024usd < 75000 THEN '3. $50,000 - $74,999'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 75000 AND family_income_2024usd < 100000 THEN '4. $75,000 - $99,999'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 100000 AND family_income_2024usd < 150000 THEN '5. $100,000 - $149,999'
    WHEN family_income_2024usd >= 150000 THEN '6. $150,000 and over'
    ELSE 'Unknown'
  END AS income_bracket,
  COUNT(*) as sample_size,
  SUM(weight) as sum_weight,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_pretty_satisfied,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 2)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_more_or_less,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 3)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_not_satisfied
FROM gss
WHERE family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL AND satfin IS NOT NULL AND weight IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

WITH deciles AS (
  SELECT 
    satfin,
    weight,
    family_income_2024usd,
    ntile(10) OVER (ORDER BY family_income_2024usd) as decile
  FROM gss
  WHERE family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL AND satfin IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  decile,
  MIN(family_income_2024usd) as min_income,
  MAX(family_income_2024usd) as max_income,
  COUNT(*) as sample_size,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_pretty_satisfied,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 2)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_more_or_less,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 3)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_not_satisfied
FROM deciles
GROUP BY decile
ORDER BY decile;

SELECT 
  CASE 
    WHEN year < 1980 THEN '1970s'
    WHEN year < 1990 THEN '1980s'
    WHEN year < 2000 THEN '1990s'
    WHEN year < 2010 THEN '2000s'
    WHEN year < 2020 THEN '2010s'
    ELSE '2020s (Web/Mixed)'
  END as era,
  COUNT(*) as sample_size,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_pretty_satisfied,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 2)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_more_or_less,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 3)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_not_satisfied
FROM gss
WHERE satfin IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1;

WITH deciles AS (
  SELECT 
    satfin,
    weight,
    age,
    wrkstat_label,
    family_income_2024usd,
    ntile(10) OVER (ORDER BY family_income_2024usd) as decile
  FROM gss
  WHERE family_income_2024usd IS NOT NULL AND satfin IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
  decile,
  AVG(age) as avg_age,
  SUM(weight * (wrkstat_label = 'retired')::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_retired,
  SUM(weight * (satfin = 1)::INT) / SUM(weight) * 100 as pct_pretty_satisfied
FROM deciles
WHERE decile IN (1, 2, 3, 10)
GROUP BY decile
ORDER BY decile;

trail.task: In the WHR dataset, how does life_evaluation relate to explained_by_gdp_per_capita? Group countries into quintiles or deciles of explained_by_gdp_per_capita for the years 2019-2025 and find the average life_evaluation for each group to see if national happiness plateaus as countries get richer.

queries.sql: SELECT MIN(year), MAX(year), COUNT(*) FROM whr WHERE year >= 2019 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL;

WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        life_evaluation,
        explained_by_gdp_per_capita,
        NTILE(10) OVER (ORDER BY explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS gdp_decile,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS gdp_quintile
    FROM whr
    WHERE year >= 2019 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    gdp_decile,
    COUNT(*) AS n_rows,
    MIN(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS min_gdp_exp,
    MAX(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS max_gdp_exp,
    AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_exp,
    AVG(life_evaluation) AS avg_life_eval
FROM ranked
GROUP BY gdp_decile
ORDER BY gdp_decile;

WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        life_evaluation,
        explained_by_gdp_per_capita,
        NTILE(5) OVER (ORDER BY explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS gdp_quintile
    FROM whr
    WHERE year >= 2019 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    gdp_quintile,
    COUNT(*) AS n_rows,
    MIN(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS min_gdp_exp,
    MAX(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS max_gdp_exp,
    AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_exp,
    AVG(life_evaluation) AS avg_life_eval
FROM ranked
GROUP BY gdp_quintile
ORDER BY gdp_quintile;

WITH ranked AS (
    SELECT 
        life_evaluation,
        explained_by_gdp_per_capita,
        NTILE(20) OVER (ORDER BY explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS gdp_vigintile
    FROM whr
    WHERE year >= 2019 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT 
    gdp_vigintile,
    COUNT(*) AS n_rows,
    MIN(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS min_gdp_exp,
    MAX(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS max_gdp_exp,
    AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_exp,
    AVG(life_evaluation) AS avg_life_eval
FROM ranked
GROUP BY gdp_vigintile
ORDER BY gdp_vigintile;

SELECT 
    year,
    CORR(explained_by_gdp_per_capita, life_evaluation) AS correlation,
    AVG(life_evaluation) AS avg_life,
    AVG(explained_by_gdp_per_capita) AS avg_gdp_exp,
    COUNT(*) AS n_countries
FROM whr
WHERE year >= 2019 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY year
ORDER BY year;
DESCRIBE whr;

SELECT country, explained_by_gdp_per_capita, life_evaluation
FROM whr
WHERE year = 2025 AND explained_by_gdp_per_capita IS NOT NULL
ORDER BY explained_by_gdp_per_capita DESC
LIMIT 5;
